citations.title: Health care service firm definition and enabling statute
citations.requirement: Defines a health care service firm as an agency that places or arranges placement of personnel for health care, companion or personal care services. A firm that does this must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs (DCA). Statute text was not fetched in this pass. This is carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Definitions (health care service firms)
citations.requirement: Defines the terms used in the HCSF subchapter. Used to confirm that the firm is in scope. Carried from the fact-checked research. Rule text was not re-read.

citations.title: Initial registration requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Register on Director-provided forms. The package includes the firm and trade names, each primary location, officers, directors and principals, owners of 10% or more, and managing agents. It also includes a criminal-conviction certification from each officer, director, principal or owner (N.J.S.A. 34:8-44), a $10,000 bond, and a list of licenses held in other states with any actions taken. The Director may waive the bond for an entity with a net worth of $100,000 or more, shown by a CPA or licensed-accountant certified financial report. (b) Give the owner and managing-agent information before any change in ownership or management. (c) Report any change to application information to the Section in writing within 30 calendar days. (d) If an officer, director, principal or owner is convicted after filing, obtain a new affidavit and file it within 30 days of the conviction.

citations.title: Registration renewal
citations.requirement: Renewal requires evidence of accreditation (in effect from May 21, 2019). Financial statements and audits under 13.5A are submitted with the renewal. Taken from the fact-checked research (50 N.J.R. 1299). Full current text was not re-read.

citations.title: Financial statements, audits, and reports
citations.requirement: (a) Submit a financial statement for the prior calendar year by July 1 each year. It must match the firm's State tax filing and be filed with the renewal. It must show assets, liabilities, gross income, operating expenses, and money received for NJ Medicaid PCA services. (b)-(c) A firm that received more than $250,000 in NJ Medicaid PCA revenue in the relevant year must file a periodic audit. (d) A firm with $10 million or more in gross income must file an audit. (e)-(f) A firm with less than $250,000 in PCA revenue and $1 million to under $10 million in gross income must file a report that includes a review by a NJ-licensed CPA. (j) Audits must have an unqualified opinion plus compliance and financial components. The law-firm summary in the research reports (b)-(e) as suspended, so confirm the current status with DCA.

citations.title: Prohibited acts
citations.requirement: An HCSF shall not: (1) recruit or advertise for staff, offer services, or contract with a facility before obtaining registration; (2) charge a fee or liquidated damages to an employee or in connection with employment, unless it also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2; (3) prevent an employee by contract from working for others, and any fee charged on that basis also requires an employment agency license; (4) knowingly send employees to, or keep serving, a facility not under NLRB jurisdiction where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers.

citations.title: Information for patient/employers
citations.requirement: (a) Every certified HHA or regulated professional must wear an ID tag at all times while giving care. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, the certification or licensure level and a photograph. Letters must be equal in size and at least 1/4 inch. The tag must be at least as large as any other ID worn. (b)-(c) Give each patient/employer the Board of Nursing's Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides at least 24 hours before services. (d) The patient may waive the 24-hour timing in writing. The firm keeps the waiver for at least 2 years and must still provide the guide before services begin.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aides and agencies
citations.requirement: (a) An agency must be licensed as an HCSF to place certified HHAs. (b) It may refer or place only actively certified HHAs it employs. (c) An HHA may perform only tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor. (d) The supervisor must ensure the HHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task. (e) The supervisor must document in the patient's record every task delegated.

citations.title: Duties relating to placements in home care settings
citations.requirement: (a) Before placement, an appropriately licensed person must evaluate the patient's needs and write a plan of care. The preparer signs it with their license designation. (b) Placements must match the level of care in the plan. (c)-(d) At least once in every 30-day period of service, the supervisor inquires whether the plan is adequate and whether it is being carried out, and records the responses. (e) If the plan needs revision, a licensed person must reassess it immediately. (f) If the plan is not being carried out properly, the agency must take corrective action immediately. (g) The supervisor makes an on-site, in-home evaluation of the plan at least once in every 60-day period. (h) The agency keeps the original and any revised plan and gives copies to the patient or representative.

citations.title: Certification of need for personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: A physician or practitioner must certify the need for PCA services in writing, at the initial application and annually. Taken from the fact-checked research. The full text was not re-read.

citations.title: Duties of the registered professional nurse (PCA)
citations.requirement: The RN assesses the beneficiary and prepares the plan of care consistent with the physician/practitioner certification. This is done at the start of service and never later than 48 hours after it. The plan lists tasks, hours, goals and the beneficiary's strengths and family needs. It is dated and signed by the PCA and the RN. The RN directly supervises the PCA in the home during the PCA's assigned time. The minimum is one visit every 60 days, with the first initiated within 48 hours of the start of service. Extra visits are made for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs. With multiple PCAs, visits rotate until all staff are assessed on each covered shift. For beneficiaries in a managed care plan, the plan completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours.

citations.title: Limitations on personal care assistant services
citations.requirement: (a) No reimbursement in listed settings, including assisted living, nursing facilities, hospitals and adult day health. (b) PCA services by a family member are not covered, except under the Personal Preference Program. No exceptions for a spouse, legal guardian or parent of a minor. Other relatives may get case-by-case exceptions requested by the agency. In that case the PCA must be a currently certified HHA, an employee of the requesting agency, and directly supervised by that agency's RN. (c) PCA is not authorized for respite, stand-alone supervision, companionship, child care, parenting tasks, mental-health service needs, non-functional diagnoses, acute short-term conditions or non-hands-on-only needs. (d) No reimbursement if the PCA lives in the beneficiary's home. (g) Maximum of 40 hours per calendar work week, prior authorized. (h) For two or more beneficiaries in one residence, combine individual hands-on hours with group hours for household tasks. (i) Unused units cannot be carried over.

citations.title: Homemaker-home health aide training program (as reproduced in the Board of Nursing Training Book, rev. 6/13/19)
citations.requirement: Training is at least 76 hours: 60 classroom plus 16 clinical in a skills lab or patient care setting. Class size is at most 30 students per instructor. Clinical supervision is by an RN at no more than 10 aides per RN. Board of Nursing written approval is required before the program starts. The Board will not certify an applicant until a criminal history check clears. Confirm that the current code version is unchanged from the 2019 Training Book.

citations.title: Definition of homemaker-home health aide (as quoted in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: An HHA is employed by a home care services agency. Under RN supervision, the HHA follows a delegated nursing regimen or performs delegated tasks consistent with N.J.A.C. 13:37-6.2. A NJ RN must supervise the certified HHA and the program of care delivered.

citations.title: Criminal history background check for HHA certification (as cited in the Training Book)
citations.requirement: All initial HHA applicants must undergo a criminal history background check. The Board of Nursing will not certify an applicant until it determines that no disqualifying criminal history record exists in FBI or NJ State Police files.

citations.title: Delegation of nursing tasks (referenced in N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2; text not read)
citations.requirement: Cited in 13:37-14.2 as the delegation provision that governs tasks an RN may delegate to an HHA. Section number confirmed only as a cross-reference. Read the full text before writing the medication and delegation procedures.

citations.title: HCSF accreditation within 12 months of registration
citations.requirement: An HCSF must obtain accreditation from a NJ Department of Human Services-recognized accrediting body within 12 months of registration. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Act concerning health care service firms and homemaker-home health aides (accreditation)
citations.requirement: Reinforces the accreditation requirement. Evidence of accreditation is required at renewal. Carried from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: 2026 HCSF law (signed July 22, 2026)
citations.requirement: Moves the annual registration expiration from June 30 to September 30. Registrations that had already renewed for 2026-2027 are extended to Sept. 30, 2027. DCA implementation guidance was pending. The source is a secondary law-firm summary, so confirm with DCA.

citations.title: State plan personal care services rate
citations.requirement: Fee-for-service PCA rate of $26.68/hour (T1019, 15-minute unit), effective 7/1/2024. MCO rates are contracted and not public. Carried from the research.

citations.title: 1915(j) self-directed PCA reimbursement methodology
citations.requirement: Sets the payment methodology for self-directed PCA services (Personal Preference Program). Carried from the research.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification mandate
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services delivered in the home. NJ's EVV aggregator is HHAeXchange (per the research). Carried from the research.

citations.title: Annual registration fee ($500 per primary location, as cited by the law-firm source)
citations.requirement: The $500 annual registration fee per primary location is cited through a secondary source. The rule text was not read. Confirm the current fee on the DCA portal.

citations.title: Board of Nursing fees
citations.requirement: Board of Nursing fee schedule, including the HHA certification application fee. The research cites $50, nonrefundable. Confirm on current Board pages.

citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the subchapter table of contents. The text was not read. Read it before finalizing the policy on uncertified individuals.

citations.requirement: The section number and title were confirmed in the table of contents. It is cross-referenced in 10:60-3.8(c)(9) for hands-on versus non-hands-on needs. The text was not read. Read it to define the PCA task list.

policies.title: Intake Interview, Initial Assessment and Post-Facility-Discharge Assignments
state_specifics: DON/HCSS assigns a nurse, office manager or other responsible staff member to interview the patient and/or family/significant other.
Facility discharges: the DON/HCSS or on-call RN takes responsibility for delegating care during the first 24-48 hours, pending the designated RN's in-person assessment.
All other assignments: an RN does an in-person nursing assessment before care starts to set a physical and functional baseline.
Medicaid PCA: RN assessment and plan of care at start of service, and no later than 48 hours after (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.5).

policies.title: Intake Interview Documentation
state_specifics: Record full name, DOB, gender, PCP/health professional name and phone, and family/significant-other name, phone and relationship.
Record past medical history, diagnoses/problems, medication list and functional status, if known.
Record services already in place, additional services needed and collateral contacts.
Intake worker prints name, signs and dates the form.
If history, diagnoses, medications or function are unknown, document the attempt to obtain them.

policies.title: In-Person Nursing Assessment
state_specifics: DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor assesses before service starts (within 24-48 hours for facility discharges) to decide which tasks may be delegated to the CHHA.
Record vitals (temperature, pulse, respiration, BP) and a pain assessment.
Record history, diagnoses, medications, functional status, psycho-social review, nutrition/diet and a systems review (neuro, musculo-skeletal, integumentary, cardiovascular, pulmonary, GI, GU).
Record home safety review with fall-risk assessment, emergency plan and advance directives.
File the PCP Certification of Need where applicable; the Nurse Supervisor dates and signs.

policies.title: Plan of Care Development, Signatures and Copies
state_specifics: Written by the DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor from the in-person assessment before service starts (24-48 hours for facility discharges).
Plan states days/hours, diagnoses/problems, tasks and frequency, assigned staff and their licensure/certification status, and short- and long-term goals including discharge.
Plan lists the specific changes in patient status the CHHA must report to the Nurse Supervisor.
Signed and dated by the assessing nurse, the patient/family/significant other, and the assigned employee at start, at each reassessment and at each plan change.
Keep a copy in the office and at the residence, available to the patient, family and employees (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(h)).

policies.title: Nurse Delegation and Practitioner Supervisor Duties
state_specifics: A CHHA performs only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor.
The supervisor ensures the CHHA demonstrates competence in each delegated task.
The supervisor documents every delegated task in the patient's record.
An NJ-licensed RN supervises the CHHA and the program of care (N.J.A.C. 13:37-14.2).

policies.title: Competency Check Before Services Start in a New Client Home
state_specifics: RN gives the assigned CHHA an in-person description and/or demonstration of delegated tasks before services start, regardless of experience.
RN confirms the CHHA has the skills and may refuse to delegate to a CHHA who lacks them.
A CHHA has a duty to refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently perform.
Document the demonstration in the client record and the CHHA file.

policies.title: Weekly CHHA Activity Records
state_specifics: CHHA completes and files a weekly activity sheet with the agency.
Sheet records date and time of each assignment, activities performed, and Plan of Care activities not performed with reasons.
Sheet records any change in condition reported to the Nurse Supervisor, documented by both CHHA and nurse.
CHHA signs and dates; patient, family, significant other or designee signs and dates.
File with the medical record for at least 7 years (adult) or 21 years (pediatric), or longer if law requires.

policies.title: Periodic Patient Review: 30-Day Contact and 60-Day In-Person Re-evaluation
state_specifics: Nurse Supervisor reviews care records regularly and contacts the patient/significant other at least every 30 days; the clinical record reflects it.
Nurse Supervisor re-evaluates in person at least every 60 days, or sooner after an interruption in service, hospitalization or facility stay, or change in condition or function.
When the plan changes, document the reasons from the review of diagnoses, vitals and pain, function, psycho-social status, nutrition, home safety/fall risk and emergency plan.
Document employees present, licensure status and skills observed, and that the plan was reviewed with the CHHA.
Document communications with the patient or family about complaints or problems; Nurse Supervisor signs and dates.

policies.title: Nurse Supervisor Observation of CHHA Clinical Performance
state_specifics: When the Nurse Supervisor directly observes a CHHA, the employee file records skills observed and how well they were performed.
Record any demonstration or instruction given and the date of observation.
Both the evaluated employee and the Nurse Supervisor sign.

policies.title: Scope of Services: What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: CHHAs perform only tasks delegated or directed by the health care practitioner supervisor and listed on the plan of care.
Medicaid PCA is not authorized for companionship, respite, stand-alone supervision or child care.
No PCA reimbursement if the PCA lives in the beneficiary's home.
CHHAs may not work privately for clients outside the agency.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Medication tasks are limited to those the RN delegates and documents under the nurse delegation rules (N.J.A.C. 13:37-6.2; read the text before finalizing).
The CHHA records and reports medication problems to the Nurse Supervisor and does not change doses or schedules.
The medication list is part of the intake and in-person assessment.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits, Continuity of Care, EVV and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care in the home; NJ's aggregator is HHAeXchange.
Medicaid PCA billed under T1019 in 15-minute units.
Notify the client and Nurse Supervisor of a missed visit and arrange coverage with a CHHA who has had the pre-start competency review.
Weekly activity sheets are separate from EVV and still required.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: The plan of care lists status changes the CHHA must report to the Nurse Supervisor.
If the plan needs revision, a licensed person reassesses it immediately (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-14.9(e)).
If the plan is not being carried out properly, take corrective action immediately.
CHHAs follow the emergency plan recorded at assessment and call 911 for emergencies.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Plan of care carries discharge goals.
Give written notice of discontinuation and a referral to other providers or the MCO/county ADRC.
For Medicaid clients, follow the PCA provider-transfer rules (N.J.A.C. 10:60-3.10; read before finalizing).
Retain the record per the retention policy.

policies.title: Employment Application and Applicant Interview
state_specifics: Every health care applicant completes a written application with name (and nicknames), contact details, NJ license/certificate number, type, authority and expiration, DOB and SSN.
List all employers for at least the preceding year with supervisor, dates, experience and reason for leaving.
Record education and training, including CPR, with dates, locations, certificates, issue and expiration dates.
Applicant signs and dates and authorizes a criminal background check.
Every applicant is interviewed; file the interviewer's name and title and the interview date.

policies.title: Reference Checks
state_specifics: Obtain at least two references, written or documented verbal; none from family or friends.
At least one must be an employer (including the immediate past employer) or an educator, such as a CHHA program instructor.
File the referent's name and relationship, dates of employment, content and reasons for leaving.
Written references: signature, title and date. Verbal: signature of the staff member who took the call and the call date.
Pre-written recommendation letters are acceptable if the agency verifies them.

policies.title: Verification of Credentials and Annual Licensure Check
state_specifics: Before placement, examine the original certificate or other reliable source and keep a copy of the current license/certificate.
Keep a copy of the Division of Consumer Affairs online verification printout confirming current status.
The agency sets a yearly date for annual credential re-verification and files the printout.
Place only actively certified CHHAs that the agency employs.

policies.title: Personnel Record Contents
state_specifics: File contains clinical competency documentation, performance evaluations, clinical supervision records and in-service attendance.
Record date of hire and malpractice policy number where applicable.
File a passport-style photo showing the face clearly, matching the photo on the ID badge.
Keep personnel files separate from client records.

policies.title: Employee Health Attestation and TB Screening
state_specifics: Health attestation form shows the Mantoux tuberculin skin test result.
Form shows rubella and rubeola immunization or serologic evidence of immunity.
File in the personnel record before the first assignment.

policies.title: Agency Orientation
state_specifics: Orientation is offered quarterly to all newly hired CHHAs within three months of hire, or sooner based on documented expertise.

Topics: infection control, blood-borne pathogens, child abuse, elder abuse, domestic violence, pain management, patient rights, HIPAA, corporate compliance, ethics (including gifts, money and financial transactions with clients), employee safety, emergency procedures and agency policies.
Document the topic outline and time spent on each mandatory topic.
Instructor dates and signs; employees sign in with name and date.
Attendance records may be electronic if retrievable and printable.

policies.title: Annual Mandatory In-Service Training
state_specifics: Offer the in-service at least once a year, or across the year, to all CHHAs.

Required topics: blood-borne pathogens, infection control, standard precautions, child abuse, elder abuse, domestic violence, pain management, workforce protection, employee safety, back safety, needle sticks, fraud and abuse prevention and corporate compliance.
The agency may accept another HCSF's documentation that a CHHA completed some or all topics.
Keep attendance records.

policies.title: Clinical Competency Testing Before or at First Assignment
state_specifics: A Nurse Supervisor tests every CHHA before or on the first assignment date.
Direct observation of delegated care for the musculo-skeletal, integumentary, GI, urinary, cardiovascular/respiratory, neurological and endocrine systems, and promotion of sleep.
If direct observation is impractical or intrusive, the nurse may ask the CHHA to describe how the task would be done.

Written, oral or observed testing of knowledge: observation and reporting, infection control, body mechanics and reportable changes, safe environment, emergencies, client needs, privacy and property, and nutrition and fluids.

policies.title: Ongoing Clinical Competency Assessment and Recordkeeping
state_specifics: Test or assess every CHHA throughout the year by direct observation with assigned patients and/or written or oral testing.
Record the CHHA's name, skills tested, date and location, an evaluation of competency, and the Nurse Supervisor's signature and date.
Record at least an annual competency assessment by the end of each year of employment.
Records may be electronic.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: The Board of Nursing will not certify an HHA until the criminal history check clears.
Obtain the applicant's authorization on the application and run the agency's own checks for non-certified office staff.
Each officer, director, principal or owner certifies criminal history at registration; report a later conviction within 30 days (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3(d)).

policies.title: CHHA Qualifications, Certification and Renewal
state_specifics: Board-approved training is at least 76 hours (60 classroom plus 16 clinical).
Certificates renew every two years; track expirations and remove lapsed aides from the schedule.
Out-of-state certifications are not valid for NJ in-home personal care.
Application fee is $50 (confirm on current Board pages).

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Pay at least the NJ minimum wage: $15.92 for most employers in 2026, $15.23 for employers with fewer than 6 employees.
Check local ordinances in Newark, Jersey City, Paterson and Trenton.
Pay overtime and travel time per federal and NJ wage law; counsel to confirm live-in and overnight rules.
Register with NJDOL for UI, disability and family leave contributions.

policies.title: Staff Conduct, Professional Boundaries and Gifts
state_specifics: Orientation covers ethics, including gifts, money and financial transactions with clients.
CHHAs may not work privately for clients.
No borrowing, loans, or handling client finances except as the plan of care allows.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator, DON/HCSS Responsibilities
state_specifics: Designate an NJ-licensed RN or physician as health care practitioner supervisor (HCSS/DON) and file a copy of the license at registration.
Report changes in owners or managing agents to DCA in writing within 30 days.
Document the roles of the DON/HCSS, Nurse Supervisors and office staff.

policies.title: HCSF Registration, Renewal, Financial Statements and Change Reporting
state_specifics: Registration is through DCA's Regulated Business Licensure Portal: $500 application fee, $10,000 bond (waivable at $100,000 net worth) and $1,000,000 general professional liability certificate.
Annual fee is $500 per primary location; P.L. 2026, c.45 moves expiration to September 30 (confirm with DCA).
Report written changes to application information within 30 calendar days.
Annual financial statement due July 1 under 13:45B-13.5A; audit provisions reported suspended, so confirm with DCA.

policies.title: Prohibited Acts and Advertising Limits
state_specifics: No recruiting, advertising, offering services or contracting before registration.
No fees or liquidated damages charged to employees unless the firm also holds an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2.
No contract terms preventing employees from working for others.
Do not send staff to a facility where a strike or lockout is in progress to replace strikers.
Do not claim accreditation before holding it.

policies.title: Placement of Aides: HCSF Licensure and Agency-Employed CHHAs Only
state_specifics: The agency must be licensed as an HCSF to place certified HHAs.
Refer or place only actively certified HHAs employed by the agency; no independent contractors.
Verify certificate status before the first shift and annually.

policies.title: Accreditation Maintenance and Loss Reporting
state_specifics: Obtain accreditation from a DHS-recognized body within 12 months of registration.
Evidence of accreditation is required at each renewal.
Report any loss of accreditation to DCA within 10 days.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance Program, Misconduct Response and Required Reporting
state_specifics: Written procedure for responding to reports of misconduct, violations of law or regulation and unethical practices.
Report safety concerns and legal violations to licensing/regulatory agencies as required by law.
Appoint a compliance officer; billing integrity audits for Medicaid claims.
Training on fraud and abuse prevention is part of the annual in-service.

policies.title: Whistleblower Protection
state_specifics: Protect staff who report unethical, fraudulent or illegal activity from retaliation.
Provide a confidential reporting channel and document follow-up.
Cover this in orientation and the corporate compliance in-service.

policies.title: Assignment by Level of Care; NJ Certification Required
state_specifics: Do not assign Certified Nurse Assistants (CNAs) or unlicensed assistive personnel to perform in-home personal care.
Licensed and certified staff must show proof of NJ licensure or certification; out-of-state certifications are not valid for NJ in-home personal care.
Match the assigned staff's credential to the level of care in the plan of care (13:45B-14.9(b)).

policies.title: Client Complaints and Grievances
state_specifics: Patients, families and staff can report complaints to the agency; log each one.
Nurse Supervisors document complaints raised at 30-day contacts and 60-day re-evaluations.
Medicaid MCO members are told how to use the MCO grievance process.
Document investigation and resolution.

policies.title: Confidentiality, Privacy and HIPAA
state_specifics: Safeguard client and employee information; disclose only as permitted.
Copies of the plan of care are kept at the residence and available to the patient, family and employees.
HIPAA is an orientation topic; sanction violations.

policies.title: Clinical On-Call Coverage
state_specifics: An RN is on call during all hours of service.
Any RN, LPN, CHHA or other clinical staff member can reach an RN for clinical questions at all times, in no less than one hour.
Publish the on-call number to staff and clients and log calls.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Give patients and families full and truthful disclosure of all fees and billing policies.
State rate, minimum visit length, cancellation terms, services included and excluded, billing terms and complaint process.
Charge no placement or other fees to employees without an employment agency license.
Medicaid PCA: no billing for services outside authorized hours.

policies.title: Caregiver ID Tags and Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides
state_specifics: ID tag worn at all times in care shows first name or initial, full surname, certification level and photo.
Letters are equal in size and at least 1/4 inch; the tag is at least as large as any other ID worn.
Give each patient/employer the Board of Nursing Consumer Guide at least 24 hours before services.
The patient may waive the 24-hour timing in writing; keep the waiver at least 2 years and still give the guide before services begin.

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Performance Improvement and Policy Review
state_specifics: Audit delegation and supervision files for every task listed, documented and signed.
Verify that only actively certified CHHAs are scheduled and that PCA clients have a current certification of need.
Review the manual annually and when rules change, and keep version control.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Give rights before services start, along with the Consumer Guide.
Clients and families receive copies of the plan of care.
Clients may refuse services and may complain without retaliation.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Provide interpreter services and accessible materials at no cost.
Do not discriminate in intake, assignment or discharge.
Document reasonable accommodations.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Orientation covers gifts, money and financial transactions with clients.
Caregivers may not accept gifts or money or use client property or accounts.
Report suspected exploitation under the abuse policy.

policies.title: Medicaid PCA Certification of Need, Authorization and Limitations
state_specifics: A physician or practitioner certifies need in writing at initial application and annually.
PCA is limited to 40 hours per calendar work week, prior authorized; unused units do not carry over.
Family PCA is not covered except under PPP.
FFS PCA rate is $26.68/hour effective 7/1/2024.

policies.title: Medicaid PCA RN Assessment and Supervision
state_specifics: RN assessment and plan of care at start of service, no later than 48 hours after.
RN supervises the PCA in the home at least once every 60 days; first visit within 48 hours of start.
Additional visits for a new PCA, nurse delegation or changed needs.
For MCO members, the plan completes the State PCA Assessment tool and authorizes hours.

policies.title: Coordination with NJ FamilyCare, MLTSS and the Personal Preference Program
state_specifics: MLTSS is delivered through MCOs; county ADRC handles intake for adults 21+.
PPP is self-directed; payment follows NJ SPA 22-0005.
Confirm MCO authorization before starting services.
EVV is required for Medicaid personal care.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Child abuse, elder abuse and domestic violence are orientation and annual in-service topics.
Staff report suspected abuse to the agency and to the proper NJ authority; DCF child abuse line 1-877-652-2873 (verify).
Insert the county Adult Protective Services intake number (verify before publishing).
Protect reporters from retaliation.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Staff report incidents to the Nurse Supervisor immediately and complete a written report.
Report changes in condition per the plan of care.
Review incidents in QAPI.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Cover infection control, blood-borne pathogens, standard precautions and needle sticks at orientation and annual in-service.
Offer hepatitis B vaccine and PPE.
TB screening and immunity are in the personnel record.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: An emergency plan is recorded in each in-person assessment.
Emergency procedures are an orientation topic.
Maintain agency continuity and disaster plans.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety, Workplace Violence and Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Employee safety and back safety are annual in-service topics.
Home safety and fall-risk review is part of the assessment.
Client transport only with written agency approval, valid license and insurance.

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep original and revised plans of care and the delegation documentation in the patient record.
Retain weekly activity records with the medical record for at least 7 years (adult) or 21 years (pediatric), or longer if law requires.
Keep waivers of the 24-hour Consumer Guide timing at least 2 years.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Report application changes to DCA within 30 calendar days.
Report loss of accreditation within 10 days.
File the annual financial statement and renewal evidence of accreditation.
Report convictions of officers/owners within 30 days.

required_items.text: Intake interview and initial assessment: the HCSF, by or through its DON/HCSS, assigns a nurse, office manager or other responsible staff member to conduct an intake interview with the patient and/or family/significant-other.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: For patients discharged from a health care facility, the DON/HCSS or RN on call takes responsibility for delegating care during the first 24 to 48 hours, pending the designated RN's in-person nursing assessment.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: For all other assignments, an RN should conduct an in-person nursing assessment of each patient before care starts, to establish a baseline of physical and functional status and the level of services needed.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Intake Interview and Initial Assessment

required_items.text: Full name of patient
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 1

required_items.text: Date of birth
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 2

required_items.text: Gender
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 3

required_items.text: Primary Care Provider and/or other health care professional contact information, including name and phone number
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 4

required_items.text: Past medical history, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 5

required_items.text: Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s), if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 6

required_items.text: List of medications, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 7

required_items.text: Functional status, if known
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 8

required_items.text: Family/Significant-Other contact information, including name, phone number and relationship to the patient
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 9

required_items.text: Identification of services in place, additional services needed, and collateral contacts, if applicable
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 10

required_items.text: Name, date and signature of person conducting intake. If history, diagnoses, medications and functional status are not known, the documentation should reflect an attempt to obtain them.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required Intake Interview Documentation 11

required_items.text: Vital signs, including temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure, and a pain assessment. This assessment is done by the DON/HCSS or an assigned Nurse Supervisor, to determine tasks to delegate to an assigned CHHA, before service starts (or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges).
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 1

required_items.text: Past medical history
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 2

required_items.text: Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s)
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 3

required_items.text: List of medications
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 4

required_items.text: Functional status
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 5

required_items.text: Psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 6

required_items.text: A systems review (neurologic, musculo-skeletal, integumentary, cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, genito-urinary)
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 7

required_items.text: Nutritional status, including diet
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 8

required_items.text: Home safety review, including fall risk assessment
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 9

required_items.text: Emergency plan
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 10

required_items.text: Advance directives
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 11

required_items.text: Primary Care Provider's Certification of Need for Services, if applicable
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 12

required_items.text: Date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor conducting the assessment
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Required In-Person Assessment Documentation 13

required_items.text: Days and hours of service to be provided to the patient. The Plan of Care is developed by the DON/HCSS or assigned Nurse Supervisor from the in-person assessment, before service starts (or within 24 to 48 hours for facility discharges).
Nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s)
Tasks to be performed by employees and licensure/registration status of the assigned employees – RNs, LPNs, CHHAs, unlicensed assistive personnel, and therapists
The frequency at which the tasks are to be performed
Short-term and long-term goals for patient care and discharge
Specific changes in patient status that need to be reported to the Nurse Supervisor
Date and signature of the nurse who assessed the patient and developed or modified the Plan of Care
Date and signature of the patient and/or family/significant-other
Date and signature of the employee who is assigned at the start of service

Date and signature of the employee who is assigned at reassessment and whenever there are changes in the Plan of Care. A copy of the Plan of Care is kept in the office and at the patient's residence, and is available to the patient, family/significant others and agency employees.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Plan of Care 10 and following paragraph

required_items.text: Before services start in a new patient's home, assigned CHHAs receive an in-person description and/or demonstration of the delegated tasks from the RN, regardless of experience level. The RN assures the CHHA has the requisite skills and may refuse to delegate to a CHHA who lacks the competencies. A CHHA has a duty to refuse a delegation he or she cannot competently carry out.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Competency Evaluation of Assigned CHHAs Prior to the Start of Services

required_items.text: Date and time of each patient assignment. The CHHA prepares and files a weekly activity sheet with the HCSF.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 1

required_items.text: Documentation of the activities performed, as well as those activities identified in the Plan of Care that were not performed and the reasons why
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 2

required_items.text: Any change in the patient's condition that was reported to the Nursing Supervisor and documented by both the CHHA and nurse
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 3

required_items.text: Date and signature of the CHHA
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 4

required_items.text: Date and signature of patient, family member, significant other or designated party. Records are kept with the patient's medical record in the office for a minimum of 7 years for an adult and 21 years for a pediatric patient, or as required by law.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Weekly CHHA Activity Records 5 and retention paragraph

required_items.text: A Nurse Supervisor evaluates care records regularly and contacts the patient and/or significant other at least every 30 days to determine whether the Plan of Care still meets the patient's needs. The clinical record reflects this evaluation.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review and Re-Evaluation

required_items.text: A Nurse Supervisor conducts an in-person re-evaluation every 60 days (or 2 months), or more often if the patient's condition warrants. More frequent re-evaluation also applies after an interruption of service, a hospitalization or facility stay, or a change in condition or functional status, or if consistent with a service agreement.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review and Re-Evaluation

required_items.text: If the nurse changes the plan of care, the documentation reflects the reasons, based on review of: (1) nursing and medical diagnosis(es) or problem(s); (2) changes in vital signs, including temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and a pain assessment; (3) changes in functional status; (4) psycho-social review relevant to the Plan of Care; (5) nutritional status, including diet; (6) home safety review, including fall risk assessment; (7) the emergency plan.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review, list 1-7

required_items.text: The re-evaluation documentation also includes: (1) name of any employees present, their licensure status, and the skill(s) observed; (2) confirmation that the plan of care has been reviewed with the CHHA; (3) any communication with patient, family, significant other or designated party regarding complaints, problems, etc.; (4) date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Periodic Patient Review, documentation list 1-4

required_items.text: When the Nurse Supervisor directly observes a CHHA's skills, the CHHA's employee file reflects: (1) the skills directly observed; (2) an evaluation of how well those skills were performed; (3) any demonstrations/instructions provided by the Nurse Supervisor, if applicable; (4) the date of the observation; (5) the signature of the employee being evaluated; (6) the signature of the Nurse Supervisor.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §II, Documentation Requirement Relating to the Clinical Performance of the CHHA 1-6

required_items.text: Applicant's name (including any nicknames), address, telephone number and e-mail address, if available. Every applicant for employment involving health care services completes a written application.
Applicant's New Jersey license or certificate number, as applicable, the type of license, the licensing authority and the expiration date of the license
Applicant's date of birth
Applicant's Social Security number

Names, addresses and telephone numbers of all employers during at least the year preceding the application, including (a) names of supervisors, (b) dates of employment, (c) work experience, (d) reasons for leaving each employer

Education and training, including the dates of training, the location where it was obtained, any degrees or certificates received, including attainment of training in CPR, and the dates of issue and expiration, if applicable
Date and signature of applicant
Authorization to conduct a criminal background check
Every applicant for employment is interviewed. The HCSF maintains documentation of the interview, including the name and title of the interviewer and the date of the interview.

Obtain written and/or appropriately documented verbal references from at least two individuals. At least one must be (1) an employer, including an immediate past employer, or (2) an educator, including an instructor from a CHHA training program, if applicable. References do not include family members or friends.

Applicant file documentation includes: (1) name and relationship to the applicant of the person giving the reference; (2) dates of the applicant's employment; (3) content of the reference, including the reasons for leaving employment; (4) for written references, the signature and title of the reference and date signed; (5) for verbal references, the signature of the HCSF staff member who obtained the reference and date of the call. Pre-written letters of recommendation are acceptable if verified by the HCSF.

Before referral or placement of a licensed, certified or registered individual, and after personal examination of the original or other reliable verification source, maintain a copy of every employee's current license, registration or certificate, plus a copy of the Division of Consumer Affairs online verification printout confirming current status.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Verification of Credentials and Content of Personnel Record

required_items.text: Health attestation form, reflecting the results of Mantoux tuberculin skin test as well as rubella and rubeola immunization or serologic evidence of immunity
Clinical competency documentation
Performance evaluations
Clinical supervision documentation
In-service attendance records
Malpractice insurance policy number, if applicable to the individual
Date of hire
Annual verification of licensure status as reflected by the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs' online verification page printout. The agency establishes the yearly date for credentials verification.
A photograph of the employee, with the face clearly visible like those required for a passport, matching the photograph used for the employee's identification badge
Provide an orientation program quarterly to all newly hired CHHAs within three months of employment, or sooner based on the CHHA's documented level of expertise.

Orientation covers at minimum: (1) infection control; (2) blood-borne pathogens; (3) child abuse; (4) elder abuse; (5) domestic violence; (6) pain management; (7) patient rights; (8) HIPAA; (9) corporate compliance; (10) ethical considerations in home care delivery, including receipt of gifts and money from clients and other financial transactions; (11) employee safety; (12) emergency procedures; (13) agency administrative and clinical policies and procedures.

Orientation documentation includes: (1) outline of topics covered; (2) length of time for each of the mandatory in-service topics; (3) date and signature of instructor; (4) name, date and signature of employees on an agency sign-in sheet. Attendance records are maintained and may be electronic if readily retrievable and printable.

Provide an in-service program at least once each year (or over the course of a year) for all CHHAs, covering at minimum: (1) blood-borne pathogens; (2) infection control; (3) standard precautions; (4) child abuse; (5) elder abuse; (6) domestic violence; (7) pain management; (8) workforce protection; (9) employee safety issues; (10) back safety; (11) how to handle needle sticks; (12) fraud and abuse prevention; (13) corporate compliance. An HCSF may accept another HCSF's documentation that a CHHA met some or all of these topics. Attendance records are maintained.

All CHHAs undergo clinical competency testing by a Nurse Supervisor before or on the first date of assignment. This includes direct observation of delegated personal care services related to: (a) the musculo-skeletal system; (b) the integumentary system; (c) the upper and lower gastrointestinal system; (d) the urinary system; (e) the cardiovascular and respiratory systems (vital signs, antiembolic stockings, oxygen assistance, positioning); (f) the neurological system (cognitive impairment, seizure disorder, post-stroke care, rehabilitation or restorative care); (g) the endocrine system (foot care, skin care and nutrition for a client with diabetes); (h) the promotion of sleep. If direct observation is impractical or intrusive, the Nurse Supervisor may ask the CHHA to describe how the task would be performed.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 1(a)-(h)

required_items.text: Written testing, oral testing or direct observation of the CHHA's knowledge and communication skills in: (a) observation, reporting and documentation of patient status and care furnished; (b) basic infection control procedures; (c) basic elements of body mechanics and functioning, and changes in body function that must be reported to the Nurse Supervisor; (d) maintenance of a clean, safe and healthy environment; (e) recognizing emergencies and knowledge of emergency procedures; (f) physical, emotional and developmental needs of and ways to work with the populations served, including respect for the patient and the patient's privacy and property; (g) adequate nutrition and fluid intake.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Prior to or on the date of the first Assignment, 2(a)-(g)

required_items.text: The clinical competency of every CHHA is tested or assessed throughout the year, through direct observation of skills with assigned patients and/or written or oral testing as in items 1 and 2 above.
required_items.cite: Best Practices §III, Clinical Competency: Testing or assessment throughout the year

required_items.text: Competency documentation in the employee file includes: (1) name of the CHHA; (2) clinical skills tested, and the date and location of testing; (3) an evaluation of the CHHA's competency; (4) date and signature of the Nurse Supervisor performing the testing. At minimum, an assessment of competency is recorded by the end of each year of employment. Records may be electronic.

Policies and procedures relating to assignment of individuals, for the appropriate level of care, authorized to provide required service, assuring that Certified Nurse Assistants (CNAs) and unlicensed assistive personnel are not assigned to perform in-home personal care services.
The requirement for licensed and certified personnel to provide proof of New Jersey licensure or certification (out-of-state certifications are not valid for New Jersey in-home personal care).
Reporting of patient complaints to the agency
Agency's response to alleged reports of misconduct, violation of laws/regulations and unethical practices
Confidentiality requirements
Protection for those reporting unethical, fraudulent or illegal activity ("whistle-blower" protection)
Reporting of safety concerns and violations of law to licensing and/or regulatory agencies, as required by law
A procedure by which an RN, LPN, CHHA or other clinical staff can reach an RN for clinical questions at all times, in no less than one hour, with an RN on call during all hours of service.
Patients and family/significant others are provided with full and truthful disclosure of all information concerning fees and billing policies.

Every certified homemaker-home health aide or health care professional regulated by the Division wears an identification tag at all times while providing care. The tag shows first name or initial, full surname, the term for the level of licensure or certification, and a photograph. Letters are of equal size, no smaller than one-quarter inch, and the tag is at least as large as any other identification worn.
Every health care service firm provides patient/employers with a copy of the Consumer Guide to Homemaker-Home Health Aides published by the NJ Board of Nursing.
The Consumer Guide is provided at least 24 hours before services are provided.
A patient/employer may waive the 24-hour timing in writing. The firm keeps the waiver for at least two years and still provides the information before services begin.
To place certified homemaker-home health aides, an agency regulated by the Division must be licensed as a health care service firm.
A health care service firm only refers or places actively certified homemaker-home health aides who are employed by the agency.
A homemaker-home health aide employed by an HCSF only performs tasks delegated by, or directed by, the health care practitioner supervisor.
The health care practitioner supervisor ensures the aide demonstrates competence to perform the client care that is delegated.
The health care practitioner supervisor documents in the patient's record every task delegated to a homemaker-home health aide.

Prohibited acts: (1) recruiting, advertising or contracting for health care services without first obtaining registration; (2) charging a fee or liquidated damages to employees (this requires an employment agency license under N.J.A.C. 13:45B-2); (3) preventing employees by contract from working for others (the same licensing consequence applies if a fee is charged); (4) knowingly sending staff to a facility where a strike or lockout is in progress, to replace strikers.

sections: I. Definitions (reference only; no policy items)

official.notes: No single official Division checklist or form lists the written policies for an HCSF. The binding rules (N.J.A.C. 13:45B-13.3 and 13.5) cover only application paperwork, which was excluded. The Division's FAQ (HCSF-FAQ-07242025.pdf) also lists only application items: registration form, fee, formation documents, criminal-history certifications, $1M liability insurance, bond, practitioner-supervisor designation, and out-of-state licenses. The only official source that enumerates policy content is the Division's advisory 'Best Practices for Health Care Service Firms' (April 15, 2014). It says it is non-binding and that the statute and rules control, even where it uses 'shall'. Organize the manual in its order: II Clinical, III Personnel, IV Administrative, with the binding rule items (13:45B-13.6, 13.7, 14.7) cross-referenced in the matching policies. Registration is submitted online through the NJ Regulated Business Licensure Portal, and policies are not part of that submission. Keep the manual available for the Division's inspection and for the accrediting body, since HCSFs must obtain DHS-recognized accreditation within 12 months of registration. I did not fetch the NJ DHS-recognized accreditation standards or the Medicaid (PCA, MLTSS, PPP) manuals, so any added requirements from those sources are not captured here. Registration timing and financial reporting are in flux under P.L. 2026, c.45, and the Division says rule updates are pending. The 13:45B-13.3, 13:45B-14.7, 13:45B-13.6 and 13:45B-13.7 text came from Cornell LII mirrors, not the NJ Administrative Code directly. The Division's Subchapter 14 PDF could not be fetched. The Best Practices item IDs use my own section/heading plus the document's list number, because the document numbers each list separately and has no global item numbers.
